MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

1. Parties
This mutual non-disclosure agreement is made between the two parties identified in the signature block, each a party and together the parties. The parties are ExampleCorp Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales, and Acme Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales, each wishing to explore a potential business relationship with the other.

2. Definitions
Confidential Information means any information disclosed by one party to the other, in any form, that is marked as confidential or that would reasonably be regarded as confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information includes business plans, technical data, product designs, financial information, customer and supplier lists, and know-how, whether disclosed before or after the date of this agreement.

3. Confidentiality obligations
Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information strictly confidential, shall use it solely for the purpose of evaluating a potential business relationship, and shall protect it with at least the same care it applies to its own confidential information, and in no event with less than reasonable care. Neither party shall disclose the other party's Confidential Information to any third party except as permitted by this agreement, and each party remains responsible for any breach of this agreement by any person to whom it discloses Confidential Information as permitted here.

4. Permitted disclosures
A party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, professional advisers, and affiliates who need to know it for the permitted purpose and who are bound by obligations at least as protective, and may disclose it where required by law, regulation, or a court of competent jurisdiction, provided it gives the other party prompt written notice where lawful. Where disclosure is required by law, the disclosing party shall limit the disclosure to the portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use reasonable efforts to protect its confidentiality.

5. Term
This agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and continues for two (2) years unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms. The parties may extend the term by a further written agreement signed by both of them.

6. Termination
Either party may terminate this agreement by giving thirty (30) days' written notice to the other party. Termination does not affect rights or obligations accrued before the termination date, and the confidentiality obligations survive for three (3) years after termination. Expiry of the term does not affect any rights or obligations that have already accrued.

7. Return or destruction
On the other party's written request, each party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of that party in its possession or control and, if requested, certify the destruction in writing. A party may retain copies it is required to keep by law and copies held in routine electronic backups, and any retained copies remain subject to the confidentiality obligations in this agreement for as long as they are kept.

8. Limitation of liability
Each party's liability is capped at twelve months of fees. Nothing in this agreement excludes or limits any liability that cannot be excluded or limited by law.

9. Governing law
This agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising from it.

10. Notices
Notices under this agreement must be in writing and are effective when delivered to the registered office of the receiving party, marked for the attention of its legal counsel. Notices may be delivered by hand, by prepaid first-class post, or by email with confirmation of transmission.

11. General
This agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding its subject matter, supersedes all prior discussions, and may only be amended in writing signed by both parties. If any provision of this agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force. No failure or delay by either party in exercising a right under this agreement operates as a waiver of that right. This agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is deemed an original.
